Game system

Table colour

The plain surface under the board, with a light grain.

Table background

Everyone at the table sees it behind the board.

Token movement

A token is one square wide. Drag a token with the Select tool to see how far it moves. Turn on Grid lines above to see the squares.

Critical rolls

Checked top to bottom. The first rule that matches wins.

Automatic conditions

Rerolls happen before bonus dice.

Results

Labels a plain roll by its total, like 10+ "Strong hit".

Credits

Thank You

Big parts of Critter VTT and Critter Sounds stand on the work of these projects and the people behind them.

Critter VTT

  • DDB Importer and ddb-proxy by MrPrimate: how content you own on D&D Beyond can come to your table.
  • Foundry Virtual Tabletop and its community systems, D&D 5e, Pathfinder 2e and Foundryborne Daggerheart: the formats Critter VTT's importers read.
  • 5e-bits and Pf2eTools: the SRD data behind the Library.
  • pdf.js by Mozilla: reading fillable PDF character sheets.
  • JSZip: table backups in one file.
  • three.js and cannon.js: the 3D dice.
  • LevelDB and Snappy by Google: the formats of Foundry's compendium packs, which Critter VTT reads itself.
  • game-icons.net: Lorc, Delapouite and everyone who drew the icons.
  • Cloudflare Workers: where Homebase can run for free.

Critter Sounds

  • Kenku FM by Owlbear Rodeo: the idea of a soundboard for tabletop games that plays straight into your voice chat.
  • yt-dlp and its contributors: music from YouTube.
  • Fluxer and fluxer.js, with LiveKit's rtc-node: the bot that plays the table's music into a Fluxer voice channel.
  • discord.js and @discordjs/voice, with @snazzah/davey for Discord's voice encryption: the same for Discord.
  • Tabletop Audio by Tim Gerrish, Incompetech by Kevin MacLeod, Freesound and Openverse (with Jamendo, ccMixter and Wikimedia): the music and sounds you can find right in the app, each credited as it plays.
  • game-icons.net: the icons on the pads and soundscapes too.
  • opusscript, prism-media and @noble/ciphers: the voice for the bots.
  • Electron and Chromium: the app around it all, with the Web Audio and WebRTC that carry the music.
